newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods up with NYMEX at close, diffs stable.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods up with NYMEX at close, diffs stable.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices were sharply higher Monday afternoon in line with jittery NYMEX bullishness surrounding crude, but differentials on the products were stable to softer, traders said.
The only discernible diff trend was on the U.S. Gulf Coast, where low sulphur diesel firmed a touch after Amoco-led selling on Friday trashed cash diffs.

Prompt and deferred USG barrels were getting done Monday at 0.95 cent under May NYMEX heating oil futures. USG heating oil prices were stable, with deals heard getting done at 1.35 cents under May futures.
Overall, as many as 400,000 barrels of middle distillate products were said to have changed hands Monday in USG markets -- not a bad volume for a day lacking any major trends, traders said.
In New York Harbor, heating oil diffs continued to be strong amid end-of-season tightness in conjunction with bonafide early spring cold in much of the Northeast.
Prompt heat was closing at 4.00 cents over May NYMEX, and Sun Co's efforts to lower the posted price to 3.10 cents over fell on deaf ears.
Also in the Harbor, as many as 100,000 barrels of prompt "A2" regular reformulated gasoline changed hands at 0.25 cent under May NYMEX.

At the USG, prompt "M1" regular conventional gasoline was getting done at levels about 0.25 cent weaker at around 2.75 cents under May futures, while "A1" regular reformulated was being similarly weaker at between 0.25 and 0.75 cent over the May print, traders said.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633
